title: Statistics for research
examples: How do I know if my result is actually meaningful?
What is the difference between a small p-value and a big effect size?
When should I use a t-test instead of something else?

explain.say: Today we look at interpreting research results carefully.
The p-value helps determine if results are due to chance.
A small p-value suggests the result is unlikely by chance alone.
T-tests compare the means of two different groups.
Effect size tells us the magnitude or practical importance of the difference.
For example, a large effect size means a big real-world impact.

faq.q: What does it mean if my p-value is greater than zero point zero five?
faq.a: It suggests the observed difference might just be due to random chance in your sample. You would not conclude a statistically significant difference.
asks: Can I say there is no difference?

faq.q: Should I report the p-value or the effect size?
faq.a: You should ideally report both. The p-value addresses chance, while the effect size addresses practical importance.

faq.q: Does a small p-value automatically mean the effect is important?
faq.a: No. A very small p-value only means the result is unlikely due to chance. The effect size tells you how big the actual difference is.
asks: Can I have significance without importance?
What if the effect is tiny but the p-value is small?

faq.q: When do I use a t-test specifically?
faq.a: You use a t-test when you are comparing the means of two groups, especially when the sample size is small.
asks: What is the purpose of the t-test?
Is this for comparing two things?

faq.q: How do I interpret the effect size value itself?
faq.a: The interpretation depends on the specific effect size metric used. You must refer to the textbook or field guidelines for context.
asks: What is the scale for effect size?
Does the number tell me the direction?

facts: The p-value is the probability of obtaining test results at least as extreme as the observed results, assuming the null hypothesis is true.
T-tests are used to compare the means of two groups when the population standard deviation is unknown.
Effect size quantifies the magnitude of the relationship or difference, indicating practical significance.
A common threshold for statistical significance is setting the p-value less than zero point zero five.

quiz.say: A researcher finds a p-value of zero point zero zero eight when comparing two teaching methods.

options.show: The result is statistically significant because it is less than the common thres
options.say: The result is statistically significant because it is less than the common thres

options.show: The effect size must be large.
options.say: The effect size must be large.

quiz.why: Because zero point zero zero eight is smaller than zero point zero five, we reject the idea that the difference was just random chance.

wrong.1: This is tempting because large effects are important, but the p-value only speaks to chance, not size.
wrong.2: This is too strong a claim; significance only rules out chance, not the practical importance of the effect.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because the p-value calculation itself is the measure of chance, not the test's validity.

quiz.say: If a t-test yields a very small t-statistic but a large effect size, what does this suggest?

options.show: The p-value must be greater than zero point zero five.
options.say: The p-value must be greater than zero point zero five.

options.show: The study might have been conducted with a very large sample size.
options.say: The study might have been conducted with a very large sample size.

quiz.why: Large sample sizes can make the t-statistic very small even if the effect size is large, due to increased statistical power.

wrong.0: A large effect size usually pushes the p-value towards significance, not away from it.
wrong.1: The combination of results suggests a need to check sample size assumptions, not necessarily that the test failed.
wrong.3: The effect size calculation is separate from the t-statistic and remains a valid measure of magnitude.

quiz.say: A study finds that Group X scores higher than Group Y, with an effect size of zero point six.

options.show: The difference is only statistically significant.
options.say: The difference is only statistically significant.

options.show: This indicates a medium to large practical difference between the two groups.
options.say: This indicates a medium to large practical difference between the two groups.

options.show: This means the p-value is below zero point zero five.
options.say: This means the p-value is below zero point zero five.

quiz.why: Effect size directly measures the practical difference; zero point six suggests the difference is noticeable in the real world.

wrong.0: This ignores the effect size, which tells us about the practical, non-statistical size of the difference.
wrong.1: An effect size of zero point six is generally considered a meaningful, non-negligible difference in many fields.
wrong.3: Effect size and p-value are independent measures; a large effect can sometimes occur with a high p-value if the sample is huge.
